clue.text: Glad rags say debt is settled, led by tabloid

indicators.note: the tabloid comes in front of the rearranged letters

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: the letters are settled into a new order, as a debt gets settled

explanation.surface: Someone finally pays off a debt, prompted by a tabloid story, and celebrates in glad rags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is settled' is the anagram signal, not a description of the debt; The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean one's finest clothes, kept for special occasions like church on the Sabbath.

clue.text: Drains baths upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside down reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: spas are baths

explanation.surface: Plumbing: baths turned upside down to empty them.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap is to drain strength or energy gradually.

clue.text: In darkness, lone maverick is something brilliantly colourful

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go into the darkness word

parts.note: night is darkness

indicators.note: an unorthodox, wayward thing, so the letters of lone are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lone maverick stands out brilliantly in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maverick' signals the anagram of lone, and 'In' puts it inside the darkness word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas-discharge tube glowing vivid red or other colours, used in shop signs.

clue.text: Fiddle with jacket removed after a dip?

indicators.note: the trimmed word comes after a
taking off the jacket strips the outer letters

parts.note: a fiddle is a violin

explanation.surface: Someone takes off their jacket after a swim, though they fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with jacket removed' strips the outer letters of the fiddle word; 'dip?' is a sauce, not a swim.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic mayonnaise from Provence, often served as a dip; the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Stake in use when son's taken up unbeatable bargain

indicators.note: in a down clue the son's letter moves higher in the column

parts.note: a bet is a stake
busy means in use, as a phone line
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A gambler lays a stake when their son takes up an unbeatable bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' lifts the S of BETBUSY up the column to sit after BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Consumer magazines label the best-value product this way, so it is a top bargain.

clue.text: Type of worm breaks up pasta dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reads the letters from the bottom

parts.note: a lob is a lugworm
gaps are breaks

explanation.surface: A worm turns up in a pasta dish, an unwelcome find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LOBGAPS. SPAG BOL is British slang for spaghetti bolognese.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for spaghetti bolognese, pasta with a meat and tomato sauce.

clue.text: Award covering debut for Oliver Reed's double in this

indicators.note: the award's letters wrap round the single letter

parts.note: OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so take the opening letter of Oliver

explanation.surface: Seems to be about the actor Oliver Reed winning an award, with his stunt double.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Reed the actor is a red herring: 'Reed' is the mouthpiece of a woodwind instrument, and this one plays with a double reed. OBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: This woodwind instrument is sounded through a double reed, two cane blades vibrating together.

clue.text: Book with Greek character and all of local life

parts.note: iota is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A book in Greek letters covering all the local life.
explanation.definitionFit: Biota is the whole of the animal and plant life of a particular region.

clue.text: Forerunner of inheritance tax said to be within Europe treaty's limits

indicators.note: the said word goes inside the two letters for Europe

parts.note: EU is the European Union
stated means said

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A tax predecessor is mentioned as falling within the limits of a European treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits' takes the first and last letters of treaty, ignoring the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: This UK tax on a dead person's property was replaced by capital transfer tax and then inheritance tax.

clue.text: Foolish talk about Yankee uniform taken separately for eye-shade?

indicators.note: the foolish talk goes round the inserted letters
the two letters go into different places in the talk

parts.note: babble is foolish chatter
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet
Y is Yankee in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Silly chatter about American uniforms, with eye shade as an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: Y and U go into BABBLE at different points: BAB-Y-BL-U-E. 'eye-shade' means the colour of eyes, not a visor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale blue, a common eye colour, so a shade of eye; the question mark flags the pun.

clue.text: Still sexy in retrospective work

indicators.note: the sexy word sits inside the reversed work
looking back, so the abbreviation for work is read backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
hot means sexy

explanation.surface: An art critic remarks that a racy piece is still on show in a retrospective exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' turns OP (opus) into PO, and HOT goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, especially one taken from a film.

clue.text: Aimlessly go from university into African republic, cycling

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the cycled country
letters are moved round from the front to the back, like a wheel turning

parts.note: Botswana is a republic in southern Africa

explanation.surface: A student leaves university to travel around an African country by bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves BOT from the front of BOTSWANA to the back, giving SWANABOT; U then goes 'into' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To swan about is to wander idly and showily, with no real purpose.

clue.text: One's limited by alternative strategy over British set of changes

indicators.note: the numeral is bounded on both sides by the strategy

parts.note: Plan B is the fallback strategy
I is the Roman numeral one
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A politician's fallback plan, overseen by Britain, is a set of policy changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' is the bell-ringers' word for sequences of rung bells; Plain Bob is one of the simplest change-ringing methods.
explanation.definitionFit: In bell-ringing a method is a set of changes, and this is a basic, widely taught method.

clue.text: It's used for brewing, though containing arsenic

indicators.note: the word for though holds the symbol inside it

parts.note: yet means though, as in 'small yet strong'
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: A brew is in use despite being laced with poison, a murder-mystery scene.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungus ferments sugars into alcohol and is essential to making beer.

clue.text: Vet popular after working in Burkina Faso once

indicators.note: once the letters have been worked on, they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A popular vet goes to work in a West African country.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the colonial and early independent name of the West African state renamed in 1984.

clue.text: Work hard, withdrawing salary to supplement income

indicators.note: the reversed word is added inside the income word

parts.note: pay is income

indicators.note: drawing back, so the word for salary is read backwards

parts.note: a wage is a salary

explanation.surface: Someone works hard, taking money out of their pay to top up their earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' reverses the salary word, and 'to supplement' puts it inside the income word.
explanation.definitionFit: To peg away is to keep working steadily and persistently at something.

clue.text: Back twist with heads the other way round: playing this should be a breeze

definitions.text: playing this should be a breeze

indicators.text: with heads the other way round
indicators.note: the first letters of the two words change places

parts.note: hind means back, as in hind legs
to warp is to twist

explanation.surface: A twisted back makes someone turn their head the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aeolian harp is played by the wind, so 'a breeze' is literally what plays it.
explanation.definitionFit: This stringed instrument sounds when wind passes over it, so playing it is effortless.

clue.text: Superficial bit of pond life breaking cover with foul play

indicators.note: the rearranged letters break into the cover

parts.note: a lid is a cover

indicators.note: foul play is crooked, so the letters of play are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pond creatures are disturbed when someone breaks a cover by foul play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' signals the anagram of play, and 'breaking' splits the cover word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-lily leaf floats on the pond's surface, so it is a superficial part of pond life.

clue.text: Live under communal arrangement that houses Catholic nun

indicators.note: in a down clue, the live word sits below
the communal word holds the Catholic letters

parts.note: a pool is a shared, communal resource
RC is short for Roman Catholic
are means exist or live

explanation.surface: Living in a commune that shelters a Catholic nun.
explanation.walkthrough: Catholic looks part of the definition, but it supplies RC.
explanation.definitionFit: A Poor Clare is a member of the order of nuns founded by St Clare of Assisi.

clue.text: Use up colour to separate each ring

indicators.note: the colour goes between the two short pieces, keeping them apart

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
a tint is a colour

explanation.surface: Instructions for colour-coding each ring, perhaps in a workshop or game.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into savings or time is to consume them gradually.

clue.text: Very unconventional ontology ignoring core aspect of thinghood

indicators.note: unorthodox, so the remaining letters are rearranged
that letter is left out of ontology
the core is the central letter of thinghood

explanation.surface: A philosopher's unusual ontology that ignores the core of thinghood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core aspect of' gives G, the middle letter of THINGHOOD; 'ignoring' drops it from ONTOLOGY and 'unconventional' rearranges the remaining ONTOLOY.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'only too pleased', the phrase means extremely or very.

clue.text: Fellows among pious, neither starting to become equal

indicators.note: neither of the two words keeps its first letter
the fellows go inside the pious word

parts.note: devout means pious
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Fellows among the devout, none of them a front-runner, are made equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neither starting' removes the first letter of both words, and 'among' puts the fellows inside the pious word.
explanation.definitionFit: To even out is to level up, so that differences disappear and things are equal.

clue.text: Newton and graduate probing existence together

indicators.note: the letters push into the existence word

parts.note: esse is Latin for being, used in philosophy for existence
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force
MA is Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: Isaac Newton and a graduate student probe the nature of existence together.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means all together, as one group.

clue.text: Witness's very pained expression

definitions.note: read as 'witness is', so the definition is the verb to witness

parts.note: ouch is what one says in pain

explanation.surface: A witness in court is visibly pained.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness to something is to attest or guarantee that it is true.

clue.text: Retract poles in wharf, stripping lead

indicators.note: the poles go inside the trimmed wharf word
the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a quay is a wharf
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Workers retract poles on a wharf after stripping off their lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripping lead' removes Q from QUAY, leaving UAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsay something is to take back or withdraw what was said.

clue.text: Person without capability or chance to cross a sea

indicators.note: the chance word straddles the other letters

parts.note: luck is chance
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: An incapable person relies on luck to get across the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame duck is an ineffectual person, or an official serving out a term without power.

clue.text: In hiding, American's perishing short of Nebraska

indicators.note: lacking, so those letters are taken off

parts.note: doggone is the American mild curse, like British 'perishing' as in 'perishing cold'
NE is the postal abbreviation for Nebraska

explanation.surface: An American, dying, hides somewhere short of Nebraska.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perishing' is British slang for damned, not dying; the American equivalent is doggone.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie doggo is old slang for to stay hidden and keep quiet.

clue.text: Ruthless iron will

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
'll is the contracted form of will

explanation.surface: A ruthless person with an iron will.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell as an adjective is archaic for fierce, cruel or deadly, as in 'one fell swoop'.

clue.text: Miss receiving uninspired blessing one's dying to hear?

indicators.note: the girl's word takes in the other word

parts.note: a lass is a young woman, a miss
trite means unoriginal

explanation.surface: A young woman gets a dull blessing that she is eager to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dying to hear' looks like keenness; read literally it is someone actually dying, who receives this sacrament.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sacramental prayers and anointing given by a priest to a person near death.

clue.text: Good to demolish snack often

parts.note: to raze is to demolish

explanation.surface: Seems to be advice that it is good to wolf down snacks often.
explanation.definitionFit: To graze is to eat small amounts frequently through the day, like a grazing animal.

clue.text: Volte-face of holy man's somewhat radical

indicators.note: a volte-face is an about-turn, so the found letters are read backwards
only some of the letters of holy man's are used

explanation.surface: A holy man performs a political about-turn and turns out somewhat radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radical' here is the chemist's sense: a group of atoms that acts as a unit, like this C5H11 group.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a radical is a group of atoms behaving as a unit; amyl is the pentyl group.

clue.text: Wake up, lean sideways and roll over?

parts.note: to come to is to regain consciousness
a ship heels when it leans over

explanation.surface: Someone groggily wakes, leans over and rolls out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the dog command 'roll over', another order a trained dog obeys, like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are commands for an obedient dog; the question mark flags the definition by example.
